newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher with most gains registered ahead of generally positive U.S. economic which again failed to give the market an added boost.
Dealers said that for the second successive day, debt markets did not respond as favourably as expected to figures showing little threat of inflation in the United States.
"I think it's a negative sign but on the other hand, it is August," said dealer, referring to the depressing effect on trading volumes of the European summer holiday period.
Guilder state loans pursued their usual track behind Bunds, basically maintaining yield spreads to Germany.
U.S. inflation figures for July at 0.2 percent were in line with forecasts while jobless claims and June business inventory data were at or near expectations.
"The figures were good for the market but everybody is a little shaken by yesterday," the dealer said of a post-data recovery on Wednesday which ran out of steam.
He said trading remains remained thin in the absence of large institutional players who are on vacation or waiting for more signs of where the U.S. market was heading.
"Tomorrow, you will see the same levels as this afternoon," he added.
Another dealer said market-makers had business in Dutch government paper to themselves, targetting the February 2007, April 2010 and January 2023 bonds.
"The long end is still bid," he said.
Pressure on shorter paper and demand for further-out dates pushed the spread between Dutch 10-year and two-year yields down to 158 basis points, compared with 173 last Friday.
The dealer saw most market interest centered on the Bundesbank's money market pact next week amid continued speculation of a hike in interest rates.
